prediction_scored: partial. Two of three parts hit: residential complaint rates were weakly related to modelled transport noise (Spearman rho 0.22; predicted below 0.25), and street and vehicle complaints were positively related to it (rho 0.30; predicted 0.15-0.45). The registered contrast missed: rent change had no association with residential complaints (0.004 per SD), so the contrast was -0.03 (95% CI -0.09 to 0.02) against a predicted +0.05 to +0.30.
settle: Neither the registered contrast nor its opposite is supported, and the deeper question, whether complaints measure exposure, cannot be answered with a transport noise model because residential complaints are mostly about neighbours. It would be settled by measured sound levels at a sample of addresses or blocks stratified by complaint rate and by demographic change: SONYC sensor Leq series (if released at block level), a DEP or DOHMH monitoring campaign, or smartphone dosimetry. With measured levels, complaints per resident can be modelled as level times reporting propensity, and propensity estimated from repeated reports of the same incident (the method of the 2025 Annals of Applied Statistics paper on 311 reporting bias).

notes:
n = 2171 2020 tracts with at least 500 residents and complete ACS change measures. 311 totals 2022-2024 in tracts: residential 1,052,123, street/sidewalk 459,165, vehicle 162,585, commercial 196,679, DEP 'Noise' 154,110, helicopter 114,024. In the joint model for residential complaints the largest coefficients were poverty share (0.21 per SD) and change in the non-Hispanic white share (0.13); modelled noise was 0.04 (-0.00 to 0.08). A secondary contrast that the registered statement names but the support rule does not use, change in non-Hispanic white share minus modelled noise, was 0.10 (95% CI 0.04 to 0.15). This agrees with Legewie and Schaeffer (2016) that complaints follow ethnoracial change, but it is reported as secondary, not as the test. For street and vehicle complaints, modelled noise (0.13) and liquor licences (0.26) both mattered, and the rent-minus-noise contrast was negative (-0.10, -0.15 to -0.04): street complaints partly track the sources the noise model contains. Commercial complaints followed liquor licences (rho 0.58). Using the energy-mean Leq in place of the class mean gave a modelled-noise coefficient of -0.02. The noise map was read from rendered tiles of the US DOT service by legend colour at zoom 12 (about 29 m pixels; deeper levels are not cached); areas below 45 dB are unpainted and were set to 40 dB. SONYC data were not used: no public block-level sound-level file was located in this session. The ACS change measures come from the Census Bureau summary files because the Census API now requires a key; 2008-2012 values on 2010 tracts were moved to 2020 tracts by land-area weights from the Census relationship file. Rents are nominal.

After critique round 1b: Settling this needs street noise (outdoor sensors) separated from neighbour noise (indoor measurement or survey). Housing form and repeat callers are not addressed.
